Usage: python -m pynakes [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Reference management engine for BibTeX, BibLaTeX, and their materials

Options:
  -V, --version         Show the pynakes version and exit.
  --install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
  --show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or
                        customize the installation.
  --help                Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  inspect       Inspect a .bib file structure.
  search        Search entries by free text, phrases, or field-scoped terms.
  analyze       Describe a bibliography: what it holds and how complete...
  coauthors     Map who has written with whom: co-author pairs,...
  lint          Validate entries and report issues (accepts multiple...
  verify        Verify entries against authoritative metadata (read-only).
  capabilities  Show what pynakes can do: a compact index, or the details...
  format        Rewrite layout only; never change bibliographic values or...
  normalize     Normalize entries: titles, authors, journals, DOIs,...
  convert       Convert a library between BibTeX/BibLaTeX dialects and...
  enrich        Conservatively fill missing metadata (modifies the file).
  init          Create or initialize a .bib library.
  scrub         Write a copy of a library with its private content removed.
  query         Save, list, and remove named selector queries → list, set,
                remove
  ref           Manage individual reference entries → add, import, show, edit,
                directive, compare, find, remove
  dedupe        Detect and merge duplicate works → check, merge
  fields        Bulk-edit fields across matching references → set, rename,
                move, append, clear, protect-title
  keys          Work with citation keys → check, generate, repair, rename,
                usage
  groups        Manage entry groups → list, list-entries, add-entry, remove-
                entry, tree, add-group, remove-group, rename-group, move-
                group, update-group
  metadata      Inspect and update library metadata → list, set, remove,
                adopt-jabref
  tex           Manage linked TeX sources and scan them for citations → list,
                add, remove, clear, scan
  asset         Fetch and validate Pinax materials → fetch, check, repair
  corpus        Operate across multiple .bib files → combine, split, batch

  Common jobs (add --json for machine-readable output):
    find a reference          search FILE "terms" | ref show FILE --where EXPR
    read entries              ref show FILE KEY | ref show FILE --key K1,K2
    change one entry          ref edit FILE KEY --field name=value
    change many entries       fields set|append|clear FILE ... --where EXPR
    add by DOI/arXiv/URL      ref import FILE ID
    check a library           lint FILE | verify FILE | dedupe check FILE
    clean up conventions      normalize FILE | layout: format FILE
    cited in a manuscript     tex scan FILE | --where used
    PDFs and sources          asset fetch FILE | asset check FILE
  Preview any change with --dry-run --diff; apply it with --expect-sha256.
  Details: pynakes COMMAND --help, or capabilities --json --command 'ref show'.

Usage: python -m pynakes ref show [OPTIONS] [file] [key]

  Show one uniquely identified reference, or triage several at once.

  With a citation key this prints every stored field of that one reference.
  With `--key k1,k2,...` it prints a compact summary of each requested
  reference instead — title, creator, date, venue, and identifiers, plus the
  abstract under `--abstract` — so a set of candidates can be scanned in one
  call rather than one invocation per key. Both forms refuse to guess when a
  key is duplicated, and the `--key` form reports every unknown key together.
  `--where EXPR` summarizes every entry the selector matches, in file order —
  `--where 'query "to-read"'` runs a saved query, and `used`/`unused` test the
  library's linked TeX sources.

  Bounded reads: `--select` returns only the named fields (the abstract among
  them); `--include materials,provenance` adds the materials available for
  each entry and the provenance the library recorded; `--max-chars` cuts long
  values and lists every cut under `truncated`. With `--key` or `--where`,
  `--limit` pages the selection and `page.next_cursor` resumes it — a cursor
  is refused once the library changes, so pages never silently skip or repeat
  entries. Information the library lacks is reported as missing (`null`,
  `missing`, `missing_fields`), never as an omission.

Arguments:
  file  Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd)
  key   Citation key to display

Options:
  --key <str>        Summarize several references at once: comma-separated
                     keys, repeatable
  --where <str>      Summarize every reference this selector matches, in file
                     order (the shared --where grammar, saved queries and
                     used/unused included); narrowed by --key
  --resolved         Include fields inherited through crossref/xdata
  --abstract         Include each abstract in the --key summary
  --select <str>     Return only these fields under 'fields': comma-separated,
                     repeatable. A selected field the entry lacks is null and
                     listed in missing_fields
  --include <str>    Also report what the library records outside the entry's
                     fields: materials (Pinax files and file links),
                     provenance (manifest records and directives). Comma-
                     separated, repeatable
  --max-chars <int>  Cut every returned text value to at most this many
                     characters; each cut is listed under 'truncated'
  --limit <int>      With --key or --where, return at most this many entries
                     per page
  --cursor <str>     Resume a paged read: pass page.next_cursor from the
                     previous page. Refused when the library changed since
  --json             Emit machine-readable JSON
  -f, --file FILE    The library to read, as an alternative to the leading
                     FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working
                     directory)
  --pretty           Indent --json output for reading (default: compact, one
                     line)
  --help             Show this message and exit.
